# Listening for structure in social life

I am a PhD student in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at Princeton University. I study how animals learn, organize, and use vocal signals—and what those signals reveal about identity, relationships, and coordination.

My work brings together animal communication, bioacoustics, vocal learning, social behaviour, and quantitative approaches to vocal sequences.

## The questions that connect my work

I am especially interested in how vocal sequences encode identity, social relationships, and coordination; how learned communication changes inside real social networks; and how quantitative methods can reveal structure beyond individual calls.

The [Research](../research/) pages introduce current and past projects. The [Publications](../publications/) page collects formal outputs, while [Notes](../notes/) provides room to explain why a question matters, what happened during the work, and what I would like to explore next.
